rationale.text: The select sits in a form, in the top-left corner of a 200 by 200 box clipped by inset(0 round 100px). The rounded corner has a radius of 100 pixels, so no part of the 10 by 10 select, at least 4 pixels square, lies inside the clip: the select is not visible, and it holds an optgroup without a label attribute. The test gives no exception for hidden lists, but it does not say whether a list invisible this way is one it covers. The custom check answers cannot_tell at step 2 (not visible: no part at least 4 pixels square inside every clipping ancestor); the form is found at step 1, so that step does not decide. Only the record supports this branch; the tool leaves it to a human. Q60 (item 1) rules that an inset() with a round part is unmeasured, so visibility is unknown and the answer is cannot_tell, never a fault; before the builder's fix the code measures the rectangle and may fault, so this case may not match the current code. The finding is needs_review at both levels: not_enabled at fail_only, cannot_tell at full.

citations.quote: Dans chaque balise `<select>`, chaque balise `<optgroup>` possède-t-elle un attribut `label` ?
